name: NL8902 (Nisshinbo JFET-input dual audio op-amp)
tagline: Nisshinbo's May 2025 JFET-input 'entry' dual built on MUSES know-how. A Japanese DIY blogger ranked it above MUSES8920 and NL8802 in listening tests.
technology: JFET-input dual audio op-amp. Nisshinbo describes it as MUSES sound technology with improved productivity. Headline claims: unity-gain stable, EMI-hardened input (EMIRR 82 dB at 1.8 GHz), 1.3 mA per channel. It is the JFET counterpart of the bipolar NL8802. Packages are SMD only: EMP-8 (AN) and DFN4035-8 (GR). No die, process or fab details are published.

part_numbers.status: active (stocked by Akizuki as NL8902AN and by Kyohritsu eleshop and Profusion as NL8902ANAE2S)
part_numbers.notes: EMP-8 package (EMP-8-AN). There is no DIP-8 version, so socket rolling needs an EMP8-to-DIP8 adapter board. The earlier draft guessed an 'AE1S' suffix by analogy with NL8802ANAE1S. The observed code is NL8902ANAE2S.

part_numbers.notes: DFN4035-8-GR package. Full ordering suffix not captured.

lineage.notes: Launched in the NL line next to the bipolar NL8802. No second sources are known. Macnica distributes it and markets it as 'a new standard for entry-level models'.

lineage.vendor: New Japan Radio (JRC) / Nisshinbo MUSES line
lineage.notes: The vendor positions it as MUSES technology with improved productivity, the NL-line counterpart of the JFET MUSES8920/8920A. JRC's older NJM8901 was described in nearly the same words, but no link between the two parts is known (open question).

reputation.summary: A new part with little coverage outside Japan. Most of the praise comes from new_western_elec (nw-electric.way-nifty.com), a Japanese DIY-audio blogger. In a Sept 2025 A/B session he ranked OPA2604 < MUSES8820 < MUSES8920 < NL8802 < NL8902, and he heard more high-frequency extension and more detail than MUSES8920. His Oct 2025 post compares NL8902 with the new MUSES8921. NS-kobo's phono-EQ listening comparison reportedly found NL8902AN better than OPA2604AP, with richer musical reproduction (known only from a search summary; the attribution is not fully certain). The distributor Macnica pitches it as entry-level with sound 'on par with higher-end models'. That is marketing. No measurements from Audio Science Review or other independent sources were found.
sonic_descriptors: more information/detail than MUSES8920 and NL8802 (new_western_elec ranking)
richer musical reproduction than OPA2604AP in a phono EQ (NS-kobo, via search summary)
typical_uses: op-amp rolling in DAC output, line and phono-EQ stages on EMP8-to-DIP8 adapters (community use)
vendor-listed uses: preamplifiers, active filters, line amplifiers, I/V conversion amplifiers
caveats: The praise comes from one or two Japanese hobbyist listeners. There are no independent measurements.
SMD only (EMP-8 / DFN4035-8). DIP sockets need an adapter board, and the adapter and layout can colour comparisons.
Only press-release typical figures are known. The datasheet min/max tables and the datasheet version were not checked.
Supply risk: new_western_elec has voiced worry about Nisshinbo restructuring and past MUSES discontinuations (blog opinion, low confidence).
Do not confuse it with MUSES8920/8920A/8921. Those are separate part numbers, not revisions of NL8902.

counterfeit_notes: No reports of NL8902 counterfeits were found. Fake MUSES-branded parts are widely reported (e.g. MUSES01 fakes). NL parts are cheaper and not MUSES-branded, so they may be less attractive to counterfeiters (inference). Nisshinbo makes the NL8902 only in EMP-8 and DFN4035-8, so any 'NL8902' sold as a native DIP-8 part should be treated as suspect. Retailers' DIP adapter modules are legitimate. Buy from Akizuki, Kyohritsu eleshop, Marutsu, Macnica or other authorized channels.

The NL8802 datasheet copy on Mouser is nl8802_s_e-3435312.pdf, marked Ver.1.0, which suggests Nisshinbo names files '<pn>_s_e.pdf'. So the inferred seeds NL8902_E.pdf and NL8902_J.pdf may be wrong. A Mouser copy of the NL8902 datasheet was not found.
Supply range: one search summary says '±4.0 V to ±16 V' and another says '4 V to 16 V dual supply'. The datasheet has to settle it.
NL8902GR (DFN4035-8): full ordering code and distributor availability were not seen.
Is NL8902 related to JRC's NJM8901 or derived from the MUSES8920 die? Unknown.
The conclusion of new_western_elec's Oct 2025 'NL8902とMUSES8921' post was not captured.
NS-kobo's NL8902AN phono-EQ remarks are known only from a search summary. Confirm the wording.

revision_chain_notes: NL8902 has one vendor document, the Nisshinbo Micro Devices NL8902 datasheet. Nisshinbo is the sole source: the part launched 2025-05-13, and there are no acquirer re-issues or second sources. The chain from oldest to newest is: (1) the initial release around May 2025, with its revision string not seen. It is probably 'Ver.1.0' by analogy with the sibling NL8802 copy on Mouser, but that is unconfirmed. (2) Any later Ver. updates are unknown. None of the search summaries showed a doc number or a 'Ver.' footer. The search found no distributor copy of the datasheet PDF (Mouser /datasheet/2/, DigiKey, alldatasheet and similar). The only new URLs are two launch news articles, from Electronic Specifier and audioXpress, and they are not datasheets. Still missing: the Ver. string and date of the first release, any later revisions and their change summaries, and a revision-specific vendor PDF URL (the PDF link on the product page was not captured). Since the part is new (2025), there are no legacy vendor URLs from earlier eras, and the only archive seed is the current product page. Search budget: 3 WebSearch calls were issued. Two returned results, and the third was refused because the session-wide budget (200/200) was used up.
